chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from Rabi' ibn Abdullah, from Al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the man who marries the woman but does not make it within himself that he would be giving her her dower, so he is an adulterer.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man marries a woman but does not intend to pay her dower?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from al-Kafi highlights that the intention (niyyah) to fulfill the core obligation of the dower is essential for the validity of the marriage contract. The ruling that such a man is considered an 'adulterer' (zani) underscores the link between contractual sincerity and sexual permissibility, a view supported by scholars who argue that deceit in the fundamental condition invalidates the union's sanctity. This emphasizes that mahr is not merely a financial transaction but a constitutive element of the marital bond.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Khalaf Bin Hammad, from Rabie Bin Abdullah, from Al Fuzayl Bin Yasaar,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding the man who married the woman but did not make it within himself that he would be giving her dower to her, so he is an adulterer’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from his father from Khalaf ibn Hammad from ibn Rib’iy ibn ‘Abd Allah from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If a man marries a woman and does not tell his soul to pay her mahr (dower) it is fornication.’”
